title: Keep the low 8 bits
starter:
let to_i8 (x : int) : int =
  x land 255
hints: `x land 255` is right for results from 0 to 127. Results from 128 to 255 should be 256 lower.
One way without an `if`: add 128 before you mask, then subtract 128 after.

answer.explain: An i8 keeps 8 bits, so 256 different values, and reads them as -128 to 127. Masking with 255 keeps the low 8 bits as 0 to 255. Shifting by 128 before the mask and back after it moves that window to -128 to 127: 200 becomes 328, masks to 72, and 72 - 128 is -56. This is what `cast X dtype=i8` does in your compiler.
